name: Lakshmana Perumal Temple, Thirumoozhikkulam
deity: Vishnu worshipped as Lakshmana Perumal — the lord of Thirumoozhikkalam in the hymns — standing in four-armed form
period: A Divya Desam of Malai Nadu by the Chalakudy river, sung by Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: By the Chalakudy river at Moozhikkulam, Vishnu is worshipped as Lakshmana Perumal — a Malai Nadu Divya Desam sung by Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar, and one of the four Nalambalam shrines of the Ramayana month.

sections.history: Thirumoozhikkalam — today Moozhikkulam, in Ernakulam district — is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Malai Nadu; both Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar sang its lord. In the age of the Chera Perumals the Moozhikkulam settlement gave its name to the Moozhikkalam Kacham, a medieval covenant on temple and land administration known from Kerala inscriptions. Today it is best known as one of the Nalambalam, the four temples of the Rama brothers — Rama at Thriprayar, Bharata at Irinjalakuda, Lakshmana here at Moozhikkulam and Shatrughna at Payammal — visited together in a single day in the month of Karkidakam.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the traditional Kerala manner: a sanctum (srikovil) beneath sloping roofs, wrapped by the nalambalam cloister, with the balikkal altar stone and the flagstaff on the approach. The riverside setting is part of its character, the Chalakudy river flowing close to the temple grounds. Within the sanctum the lord, worshipped as Lakshmana, stands in the four-armed form of Vishnu, receiving the worship of the Kerala rite.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the sage Harita performed penance here, and that Vishnu appeared and blessed him with sacred teaching — the 'thiru mozhi', the holy word, that tradition hears in the name Thirumoozhikkalam. Kerala tradition also holds that the four images of the Nalambalam, once worshipped far away, came ashore on the Kerala coast and were enshrined by a local chieftain, each brother in his own temple — Lakshmana here, beside the river.
sections.festivals: The temple's annual festival is kept with flag hoisting and processions, and Vaikunta Ekadashi is observed. Its busiest season, though, is Karkidakam (July–August), the Ramayana month, when pilgrims make the Nalambalam darshan, visiting the shrines of Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna in order on a single day.
sections.experience: Come in Karkidakam to join the Nalambalam pilgrims, or in another season for a quieter darshan by the river. The traditional order runs from Thriprayar to Irinjalakuda, then Moozhikkulam and Payammal, ideally completed before the temples close at midday. Sit a while by the Chalakudy river and remember the Alvars, who sang this lord long before the pilgrimage took its present form.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure, following the temple's own schedule; festival days are crowded. Confirm current timings locally before you visit.
visit.dressCode: Traditional dress is expected: by Kerala temple custom men usually enter bare-chested in a mundu or dhoti, and women in saree or other traditional dress; footwear is left outside. Follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.gettingThere: Moozhikkulam lies near the Chalakudy river in Ernakulam district and is reached by road from Aluva or Angamaly. Both towns have railway stations, and Cochin International Airport at Nedumbassery is close by.
